audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Riposte as a parry that stuns whatever it blocks — wants.foe[1] says she can 'Parry (W) your Petrifying Gaze or a primed Twin Fang to stun you mid-combo', and whys[6] repeats it. Riposte only stuns if it blocked an immobilising effect. Blocking Twin Fang gets you slowed, not stunned.
audit.why: Riot's Riposte text: 'Fiora parries all incoming damage and disables for a short time, then stabs in a direction. This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' That distinction is the entire sequencing rule of the matchup: Petrifying Gaze is the one thing in Cassiopeia's kit that upgrades her parry into a stun, so leading with R is uniquely punished while leading with poison is not. Written the current way, a player thinks every ability is equally unsafe into Riposte and never learns the actual order to cast in.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1], whys[6], the mid text, the cooldown block, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now state that only an immobilise upgrades the parry to a stun, so the rule is bait with an auto or a Q, never with R.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d tells you to 'take the fifteen-second invitation' after Fiora burns Riposte. Riposte is 24s at rank 1 and 16s only at rank 5. No other cooldown appears on the page either.
audit.why: Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16s and Lunge is 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6s. Twenty-four seconds at rank 1 is a much bigger window than fifteen and it is the window the whole Cassiopeia game plan lives in — she casts Noxious Blast every 3.5s and Twin Fang every 0.75s, so a spent Riposte is worth an enormous number of casts. Understating it by nine seconds makes players commit too briefly and back off while they were still safe.
audit.corrected: Riposte's 24s at rank 1 and Lunge's 13s stated in the cooldown block, do's, don'ts, mid text, all-in windows and key interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Cassiopeia Level 1 and the two-item stage while the prose gives Level 1 to Fiora outright and calls two items a coinflip, and it marks Levels 4-5 and First item as Skill where the prose says Cassiopeia wins both. The diff label reads HARD while diffRating is 7/10 and breakdown.difficulty says 'Tricky matchup'.
audit.why: spikes[0] is headed "Fiora's only real window" at Lvl 1 and the early text opens 'Level 1 is hers'. whys[3] says you out-DPS her in any extended trade at 4-5 and whys[5] says you shove her off the wave at first item. whys[6] ends 'a coinflip on her cooldown'. That is Fiora, Skill, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Skill — the chart in the source packet. On the Akshan page the same 7/10 diffRating carries the label TRICKY, which is also what this page's own breakdown.difficulty says.
audit.corrected: win[0]=Fiora, win[1]=Skill, win[3]=Cassiopeia, win[5]=Cassiopeia, win[6]=Skill, phase sides matched, diff set to TRICKY.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is mentioned once, as 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', with the wrong pronoun and without naming what heals her.
audit.why: Two sources: Duelist's Dance restores health every time she hits a Vital, and Grand Challenge heals Fiora and her allies if she hits all four Vitals or the target dies after one. Against a Cassiopeia with no resistances, the two-item duel is decided by whether that healing is cut, so the item line should name the ability rather than say 'his sustain'.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now names Duelist's Dance, and the late text and the two-item spike say anti-heal is not optional.

edits.before: This is your window. With ranks in Q and E you out-DPS her in any extended trade — W to ground her dash, Q to prime, then spam refunding Twin Fangs while your boots-free Serpentine Grace speed keeps you at the lip of her Q range. At 6 your Petrifying Gaze beats her vital-dance: if she commits forward facing you, stun and burst before her R repositions her. edits.after: This is your window. With ranks in Q and E you out-DPS her in any extended trade — W to ground Lunge, Q to prime, then spam refunding Twin Fangs while your boots-free Serpentine Grace speed keeps you at the lip of her dash range. At 6 your Petrifying Gaze beats her vital-dance: if she commits forward facing you, stun and burst before her R repositions her. The one thing that flips it is Riposte — it stuns you if it blocks your R, so hold the ult until her 24s W is spent.

edits.before: You still win the straight kite when she has to walk through your poison, but this is where she gets scary — her passive vitals deal percent-max-HP true damage that your glass, resistance-free build can't tank, and one parried R or Twin Fang gets her on top of you. Keep W down to deny the dash and never duel her in a sidelane 1v1 once she has Triforce and a parry charge up. Group, zone with your range, and force her to fight into your team instead of you alone.

notes: Riot's Duelist's Dance text describes only the heal and the move speed on a Vital hit and says nothing about the damage type. The content layer calls the vitals 'percent-max-HP true damage'; the kit does carry a trueDamage flag, but on Grand Challenge rather than on the passive. I left those strings alone rather than restate or delete a damage claim the local data cannot settle either way. Lunge applies on-hit effects, which the _missing-interactions file flags as an itemisation point — it is real, but it is an argument about armour and attack speed that does not change anything a boots-less, resistance-free Cassiopeia builds, so I only recorded it in the cooldown block rather than spending length budget on it elsewhere.
